subject: math
source: English National Curriculum — Mathematics programmes of study: key stage 2 (Year 5), DfE 2013

objectives: Read, write, order and compare numbers to at least 1,000,000
Determine the value of each digit
Count forwards and backwards in steps of powers of 10
Round any number up to 1,000,000 to the nearest 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000
Interpret negative numbers in context
Count forwards and backwards through zero

weeks.topic: Roman numerals to 1,000 and reading years
objectives: Read Roman numerals to 1,000 (M)
Recognise years written in Roman numerals
Solve number problems involving place value and rounding
keywords: I V X L C D M

weeks.topic: Written addition and subtraction with more than 4 digits
objectives: Add and subtract whole numbers with more than 4 digits using columnar methods
Use exchanging accurately
Check answers using the inverse operation

weeks.topic: Mental calculation, estimation and multi-step problems
objectives: Add and subtract mentally with increasingly large numbers
Use rounding to check answers and judge accuracy
Solve multi-step addition and subtraction problems in context
Identify multiples and factors, including all factor pairs of a number
Find common factors of two numbers
Use factor knowledge to solve problems
Know prime numbers, prime factors and composite numbers
Establish whether a number up to 100 is prime
Recognise and use square (²) and cube (³) numbers
Multiply and divide whole numbers by 10, 100 and 1,000
Multiply and divide decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000
Explain how digits move between place-value columns
Multiply numbers up to 4 digits by a 1-digit number using a formal method
Multiply up to 4 digits by a 2-digit number using long multiplication
Multiply mentally using known facts
Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a 1-digit number using short division
Interpret remainders appropriately for the context
Divide mentally drawing on known facts
Solve comparison, sum and difference problems using a line graph
Complete, read and interpret timetables and two-way tables
Choose a sensible scale for a line graph
Measure and calculate the perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes in cm and m
Find missing lengths in compound shapes
Solve perimeter problems in context

weeks.topic: Area of rectangles and estimating irregular areas
objectives: Calculate and compare the area of rectangles using cm² and m²
Find the area of compound rectilinear shapes
Estimate the area of irregular shapes by counting squares

weeks.topic: Multiplication and division problems: scaling and rates
objectives: Solve problems using multiplication and division, including scaling by simple fractions
Solve simple rate problems
Choose the correct operation in word problems

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: number, calculation, perimeter and area
objectives: Revisit place value, rounding and negative numbers
Practise the four operations with formal methods
Consolidate perimeter and area problems
Identify, name and write equivalent fractions of a given fraction
Represent equivalent fractions visually, including tenths and hundredths
Simplify fractions using common factors
Compare and order fractions whose denominators are multiples of the same number
Use number lines to place fractions
Explain comparisons using equivalent fractions
Recognise mixed numbers and improper fractions
Convert from one form to the other
Write mathematical statements > 1 as a mixed number
Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
Add and subtract fractions whose denominators are multiples of the same number
Solve problems with mixed numbers
Multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers
Use diagrams to represent the multiplication
Find a fraction of an amount
Read and write decimal numbers as fractions (e.g. 0.71 = 71/100)
Recognise thousandths and relate them to tenths and hundredths
Identify the value of each digit in numbers with three decimal places
Round decimals with two places to the nearest whole number and to one decimal place
Read, write, order and compare numbers with up to three decimal places
Solve problems involving decimals to three places
Add and subtract decimals, including money and measures
Use complements to 1 (e.g. 0.83 + 0.17 = 1)
Line up decimal points in column methods
Recognise the per cent symbol (%) and understand it as parts per hundred
Write percentages as a fraction with denominator 100 and as a decimal
Shade and identify percentages on hundred squares
Know equivalents of 1/2, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5 and 4/5
Solve problems needing these equivalents
Find simple percentages of amounts

weeks.topic: Angles: measuring, drawing and angle facts
objectives: Identify acute, obtuse and reflex angles and compare them
Draw and measure angles in degrees using a protractor
Know angles on a straight line (180°) and around a point (360°)

weeks.topic: Mid-year assessment: number, fractions, decimals and angles
objectives: Show fluency in arithmetic and formal written methods
Apply reasoning to fractions, decimals and percentages
Solve angle and measurement problems

weeks.topic: Properties of 2-D shapes: regular and irregular polygons
objectives: Distinguish between regular and irregular polygons
Use properties of rectangles to find missing lengths and angles
Reason about equal sides and angles
Identify 3-D shapes, including cubes and cuboids, from 2-D representations
Match nets to 3-D shapes
Describe faces, edges and vertices

weeks.topic: Position and direction: reflection and translation
objectives: Identify, describe and represent a shape after reflection or translation
Use coordinates in the first quadrant
Know that a shape does not change after these transformations
Convert between km and m, m and cm, cm and mm, g and kg, l and ml
Use decimal notation for measures
Solve problems involving unit conversion
Understand approximate equivalences between metric and imperial units
Use inches, pounds and pints in context
Compare measurements in different units
Estimate volume using 1 cm³ blocks to build cuboids
Estimate capacity (e.g. using water)
Compare volumes of different cuboids
Solve problems converting between units of time
Calculate durations across hours and days
Use timetables to plan journeys

weeks.topic: Money and multi-step problems across measures
objectives: Solve multi-step problems with money and measures
Use all four operations including decimals
Explain and check solutions
Show fluency across Year 5 number and calculation
Apply reasoning to geometry, measures and statistics
Solve unfamiliar problems

weeks.topic: Year 5 review and readiness for Year 6
objectives: Revisit areas of difficulty from the end-of-year assessment
Consolidate times tables and formal methods
Preview long division and fractions for Year 6
